text.p: Commodities of Australian interest were mostly weaker offshore, with base metal prices, gold and wheat all easing.
Three-months copper explored the bottom of its recent price range, although it bounced from its lows in the afternoon and finished just $8 easier at $2,231.
Dealers said volumes were light due to the Copper Club activities in New York this week, and the market exhibited no fresh features.
"Copper held at the $2,222/25 support level. It had a strong rally last week to $2,270 and now it has come back to the bottom of its range," a dealer noted.
The market was waiting for Tuesday's LME copper stocks data, which showed a sharp rise on Friday of 15,325 tonnes, he added.

Aluminium tumbled below the $1,600 support level early in the day following Friday's weak close in a move that encouraged fund liquidation. Aluminium closed at $1,585, a decline of $18 against Friday's kerb close. First support was seen just around the corner at $1,580.
Lead and zinc also bore the pain of fund liquidation although they also came off their lows, dealers said.
Lead tumbled more than $25 from Friday's kerb close to just under $650, hitting a fresh 15-1/2 month low. It then bounced on light shortcovering and finished the day at $657, down $18.
Zinc, last at $1,175, rebounded from the day's lows of $1,166. But it was still $8 lower and vulnerable to the downside.

Nickel, showed greater resilience following early weakness and finished at $7,835, a gain of $35. Early profit-taking and speculative liquidation had initially driven nickel to below $7,700 before it bounced higher, boosted by expectations of a inventory drawdown on Tuesday.
Tin was also firmer, ending the kerb at $5,920, up $45. But alloy was last quoted at $1,495/50, versus $1,520/25.

New York precious metals futures ended firmer for the second session in a row Monday, except for gold, which remains the weakest contract in the complex, traders said. "Activity was light but support for silver and further gains for platinum and palladium may eventually help gold to bounce also," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said. COMEX April gold ended down 90 cents at $343.10 an ounce, but held above the contract low at $339.40 seen Friday.

Late fund selling, led by Rosenthal Collins' sale of one million bushels, drove CBOT March wheat futures to close lower after setting a new contract low, with the rest of the market mixed, traders said. Sell stops were hit in the waning 30 minutes of trading and March dropped to a new low of $3.52 per bushel, below the previous low of $3.54-1/2 which was set Friday. CBOT wheat futures closed 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower to three higher, with March down 3-1/2 at $3.52-1/2.

NYMEX prompt heating oil remained firm Monday afternoon on short covering, bucking declines in oil prices which fell for the fifth consecutive session. "You had a lot traders who were short the heat crack who are now covering, so crude is being sold for heating oil," said a New York crude trader. "Buying in the March and selling April seems to be the feature of the day," said a New York heating oil dealer, noting there was short covering in outright heat as well. Crude and gasoline continued to be buffeted by fund selling, with March open interest declining sharply in crude. March crude was down three cents a barrel at $22.43.
